title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Part II of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. Grothendieck studies the arithmetic extension attached to the projective line minus three points, 1 → Γ̂^+_{0,3} → M'^~_{0,3} → Γ'^~_Q → 1. Here Γ̂^+_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, free on two generators ρ, σ. Γ'^~_Q is his combinatorial substitute for Gal(Q̄/Q), a GT-hat-type group. M'^~_{0,3} is the corresponding 'arithmetic' group, a profinite analogue of π_1^arith.

The previous page defines when a surjection ψ: Γ̂^+_{0,3} → G onto a finite group G is 'effective'. Write ρ_G = ψ(ρ) and σ_G = ψ(σ). Effective means: for every u in M'^~_{0,3}[0], the pair (ξ_G, η_G) obtained by applying ψ to the defining data u(ρ) = ξρ, u(σ) = ησ lies in Σ^eff_{ρ,σ}. That is, there is an automorphism u_G of G with u_G(ρ_G) = ξ_G ρ_G and u_G(σ_G) = η_G σ_G. Equivalently, ψ∘u = u_G∘ψ, i.e. the whole group M'^~_{0,3} stabilises Ker ψ. In dessin language: the dessin (G, ρ_G, σ_G) is stable under the whole GT-type action.

Theorem on this page: if ψ is surjective and effective, there is a unique homomorphism ψ_M: M'^~_{0,3} → M°_{ρ_G,σ_G} =: M°_ψ. Here M°_ψ is a finite group built from G and its distinguished generators. It is pinned down by the requirement that the elements u_{α,β,f} map to the element of M°_ψ with invariants ψ(α), ψ(β), ψ(f). These u_{α,β,f} are parametrised by α, β, f in Γ̂^+_{0,3} satisfying the 'flattened' (aplaties) loop equations. A marginal insertion says ψ_M induces a map S_0 M_{0,3} → S_0 M°_ψ. An earlier commutative-square formulation was crossed out.

Corollary: a morphism of short exact sequences from 1 → Γ̂^+_{0,3} → M'^~_{0,3} → Γ'^~_Q → 1 to 1 → G → M°_ψ → Γ°_ψ → 1. The middle vertical arrow is ψ_M and the left one is ψ.

The next page makes ψ_M explicit through three homomorphisms:
- Ψ_{T_ρ} and Ψ_{T_σ}, from Γ'^~_Q to T_ρ and T_σ. These are cyclotomic-type characters modulo the orders of ρ_G and σ_G.
- Ψ_G: M'^~_{0,3} → G_{ρ,σ}.

The three must agree in a common quotient γ_{ρ,σ}. So Γ°_ψ is a fibre product, and conjugation compatibility holds: int(x) on the source corresponds to int(U) on G.

In modern terms: to each GT-stable finite dessin / normal subgroup N of F̂_2, attach a finite quotient of GT-hat (and of its 'arithmetic π_1' extension) through which the action factors. Its elements are described by reductions mod N of the parameters (λ, f), subject to the loop equations reduced mod N. This is a finite-level 'shadow' of GT-hat, and the finite analogue of the representation of Gal(Q̄/Q) on a Galois-stable dessin and its monodromy group.
errors: 'si u = M'^~_{0,3}' should read 'si u ∈ M'^~_{0,3}'.
The equation number (72) is used twice: once for the crossed-out diagram and once for the corollary's diagram.

Uniqueness of ψ_M is asserted from its values on the elements u_{α,β,f}. This is only justified if every element of M'^~_{0,3} is of this form, or if they generate it topologically. This is not stated on the page; presumably it was established earlier.
Whether the 'flattened' loop equations suffice for the stated invariants to define an element of M°_ψ is not checked here; it depends on the definition of M°_ψ given earlier.

ideas.what: For a finite quotient of F̂_2 = π̂_1(P^1 minus 3 points) whose kernel is stable under the GT-type group, the action factors through a finite group described by reducing the parameters (λ, f) / (α, β, f) modulo the kernel.
ideas.modern_name: Finite quotients of GT-hat attached to GT-stable normal subgroups; GT-shadows / the groups GT(N) for 'isolated' N
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dolgushev, Le, Lorenz, 'What are GT-shadows?' (c. 2021) and subsequent papers; related ideas in Harbater–Schneps and in work on Galois action on dessins (Schneps, Lochak)
ideas.where_published: Not in the Esquisse d'un programme or La Longue Marche as circulated, to my knowledge; unsure about other circulated manuscripts

ideas.what: A morphism of exact sequences from the arithmetic extension 1 → π̂ → M'^~ → Γ'^~_Q → 1 to a finite extension 1 → G → M°_ψ → Γ°_ψ → 1 attached to an effective dessin.
ideas.modern_name: Finite-level ('monodromy group with arithmetic structure') representation of GT-hat on a stable dessin; analogue of π_1^arith → Aut-extension of the monodromy group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Galois-theoretic version standard (Belyi, Grothendieck's Esquisse, Matzat/Malle on rigidity, field of moduli); GT version implicit in Ihara, Drinfeld, Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Galois action on dessins but not this GT-finite-level construction

ideas.what: Effectivity criterion: every u lifts to an automorphism u_G of G sending ρ_G to ξ_G ρ_G and σ_G to η_G σ_G, equivalently Ker ψ is stable.
ideas.modern_name: GT-stability / isolatedness of a normal subgroup; liftability of GT-shadows

ideas.what: Γ°_ψ described as a fibre product of cyclotomic-type quotients T_ρ, T_σ and an automorphism quotient G_{ρ,σ} over a common quotient γ_{ρ,σ} (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the cyclotomic character mod the orders of the branch-cycle generators with the action on the monodromy group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in branch-cycle arguments (Fried); GT version less standard

missed.claim: Grothendieck constructs, for each GT-stable ('effective') finite quotient of the 3-punctured-sphere group, a finite quotient of his GT-type group Γ'^~_Q and of the arithmetic extension M'^~_{0,3}. Its elements are defined by the reduced invariants ψ(α), ψ(β), ψ(f) satisfying flattened loop equations. This anticipates the GT-shadow programme (Dolgushev–Le–Lorenz) by about 35 years. It also includes the extension level (M°_ψ, with G as kernel), not only the quotient of GT-hat.
missed.quote: alors ψ_M(u) est l'élément de M°_ψ défini par les invariants ψ(α), ψ(β), ψ(f)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: GT-shadow research is active, with computations of GT(N) for many N. Grothendieck's extension-level version (a finite group M°_ψ fitting into a morphism of exact sequences) and his effectivity criterion could supply a natural framework: an 'arithmetic monodromy group' of a dessin defined purely combinatorially via GT. This would be comparable with the genuine Galois arithmetic monodromy group.

missed.claim: The comparison between Γ°_ψ (the GT-defined finite quotient) and the image of Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on the dessin is implicit but not addressed. So is the question of whether Γ'^~_Q maps onto Γ°_ψ.
missed.quote: On a donc des homs de suites exactes (72)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing GT-finite quotients with Galois-finite quotients for stable dessins is a concrete way to probe whether GT-hat equals Gal(Q̄/Q). This is exactly the motivation of the GT-shadow programme.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a clean, finished statement: a finite-level, extension-level representation of Grothendieck's GT-type arithmetic group on effective (GT-stable) dessins. It anticipates the recent 'GT-shadows' framework. The general idea of GT acting on dessins is well known, and the statement is a natural one, so it is notable rather than astonishing.
transcription_corrections: The map is written ψ (psi), ψ = ψ_G, not φ = φ_S; similarly ψ_M and ψ_Γ.
The source group is Γ̂^+_{0,3} (consistent with the previous page) or a script-G variant of it, not 'Ŝ^+_{0,3}'.
The target subscripts read M°_{ρ_G,σ_G}, not M_{β_S,τ_S}; the parenthetical gives '(dés = M°_ψ)'.
The rotated margin note reads approximately 'en fait(?) induit un hom ... S_0 M_{0,3} → S_0 M°_ψ'. It is a marginal insertion, not in-line text.
The final line reads '(L'hom. ψ_M s'explicite : l'énoncé de trois homomorphismes', continued on the next page.
